newsitem.title: USA: Canada's Eggleton would like Helms-Burton repealed.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Eggleton would like Helms-Burton repealed.

text.p: Canadian Minister for International Trade Art Eggleton said on Tuesday he would like to see Washington's Helms-Burton law repealed but doubts that will happen anytime soon.
"Eventually, I'd like to see the legislation repealed but I don't think that's going to happen in the short-run," said Eggleton speaking to reporters at a luncheon here.

The Helms-Burton law, which has been condemned by all major U.S. trading partners including Canada and Mexico, allows U.S. citizens to sue foreign firms that invest in property that Cuba's communist government confiscated after the revolution in 1959.
Eggleton said Helms-Burton sets a "very dangerous precedent. If the United States government gets away with doing this, it can do it in other cases."

Turning to the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), Eggleton said the U.S. trade representative and the administration need to get the message out about NAFTA's benefits for trade between the U.S. and Canada.
To continually focus thoughts about NAFTA on Mexico is "dead wrong". The free trade relationship with Canada has been very productive and benefical, with millions of jobs generated on both sides.
"We paid a price for it (NAFTA) in terms of the adjustment but now we're beginning to see a lot of benefits," Eggleton added.
